newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-WEEK AHEAD-Australian markets seen mixed.

text.p: A vacuum of economic data for both the local and U.S. markets sees Australian currency and bond traders left pondering longer term issues this week.

Key local economic events this week include the October merchandise imports data on Tuesday and September quarter company profits data on Thursday. In the U.S. markets, focus will be on fresh Treasury supply on Tuesday and second tier data including housing starts later in the week.

Analysts said none of this data was likely to have any major impact on local markets. "What precious little news there is is unlikely to unwind the current bullish tone in U.S. credit markets in the wake of last week's PPI and CPI data," said Westpac economist, John Peters in a weekly economic update.

Equity markets are seen still focusing on the Dow's remarkable rise after it closed at an eighth-straight record high on Friday. Australian shares are likely to start the week on a positive note especially after base metal prices continued their recovery on the London Metal Exchange on Friday.
However, traders are becoming increasingly nervous abot a possible Dow pullback.
On bond markets, a quiet morning is expected after U.S. treasuries slipped slightly on profit-taking on Friday.
The Australian dollar is also seen subdued early after little interest was shown in the currency during the New York timezone trade on Friday.
BONDS (Friday: 10 yr cash yield 7.07 pct, 3 yr 6.58 pct)
The bond market faces another quiet week for economic indicators, although traders believe a Treasury bond tender will be announced on Monday which could set the tone for the first part of the week.
Traders said local economic data due this week was unlikely to have major market implications or have capacity to reverse the current very positive tone in local interest rate markets.

The Treasury said recently that it was aiming for a further two fixed-interest bond tenders before the end of the year and would be looking to top up the September 2009 stock to bring it up to a more liquid level. This bond was first offered at the last tender on October 29 when some A$600 million was issued.
Traders expect a shorter dated issue will be included with the 2009 offering for a tender on Tuesday.

Some traders feel the tender will be a good test of demand for the market given that last week's rally of some 15 basis points to 33-month lows at the long end of the curve was partly due to a rallying U.S. Treasury market.

However, others said the advance, which took the 10-year bond yield close to 7.0 percent, was backed by strong interest from offshore investors in the past week, leaving the market short of stock, and allowing for supply to be easily absorbed.

Initial trading on Monday should start with an slightly negative bias after U.S. Treasuries dipped a touch on profit-taking on Friday. The benchmark U.S. 30 year Treasury bond yield fell about half a point to 6.46 percent.
AUSTRALIAN DOLLAR (Fri: US$0.7909, New York US$0.7906)
The Australian dollar is expected to continue last week's slow recovery which saw it recover from a dangerously low US$0.7820 to top 79 cents on Friday.
The unit held its levels in New York trading on Friday.

Resistance was expected to be tough at US$0.7920, but dealers felt it could be breached if the market saw anything like a repeat of the more than A$1.0 billion worth of yen/A$ dual currency samurai bonds issued this week.
A break here would open the way for a re-test of October's US$0.7985 high, although few thought a rally above 80 cents could be sustained while the market wound down for year-end.

The currency would also be restrained by the risk of another easing in official interest rates, which analysts reckoned as an even chance by March next year. "Our rate view is currently close to the market view of the interest rate outlook - possibly another cut in the March quarter but no further cuts beyond the March quarter," the ANZ Bank's weekly Treasury Update said.
The data next week were unlikely to help clarify the monetary policy much, although imports might hold indirect clues on the state of business investment.

Analysts are concerned a slowdown in capital imports in the last few months may mean investment is failing to meet the government's exacting forecast of 14 percent growth in 1996/97. Another weak outcome for capital imports could fuel speculation another policy easing would be needed before too long.
AUSTRALIAN STOCKS (Fri: All Ordinaries 2,387.3, up 24.8)

Most factors are seen stronger for the Australian share market early this week with the Dow finishing last week with its eighth consecutive record closing high and base metal prices showing continuing signs of improvement. However many dealers believe the Dow is overdue for a significant correction and this would likely be reflected in the local market.

"I believe the Dow is going to have a correction. It's topping out now and that's what you would expect after a lengthy number of record runs," said Kevin Lourey, a dealer at Melbourne broker, Peake Lands Kirwan.
Market focus is likely to remain on the resources sector, dealers said, especially after the price of copper finished at a 2-1/2 month high on the London Metal Exchange on Friday.
Major resource issues the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and MIM Holdings Ltd are seen leading the market higher on Monday due to their big exposure to the copper price.

Dealers said there was little in the way of significant economic data due out next week both locally and overseas but that traders would monitor the U.S. bond market closely, especially in view of the Dow's recent remarkable run higher. The annual meeting season continues witha a number of key companies holding meetings this week.
Building products group Boral Ltd and department store chain David Jones Ltd hold annual meetings in Sydney today.
Entertainment group Village Roadshow Ltd and nickel producer QNI Ltd holds its meeting in Brisbane on Tuesday.
Qantas Airways Ltd holds its annual meeting in Melbourne on Wednesday while entertainment and leisure group Hoyts Cinema Group Ltd has its annual meeting in Sydney on Thursday.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 373-1800
